topic: Advanced Use of the C Preprocessor for Conditional Compilation and Macro Tricks
explanation: In advanced C programming, the preprocessor is leveraged beyond simple macro definitions to implement complex compile-time logic, conditional compilation, and macro tricks that enable code flexibility, portability, and optimization. Mastery of preprocessor directives allows developers to create highly adaptable code that can change behavior based on environment, compiler, or configuration, while avoiding common pitfalls such as macro side effects or token pasting issues.

extraction_metadata.source: Expert C Programming: Deep C Secrets

book: Expert C Programming: Deep C Secrets
code_example:
#define DEBUG_LEVEL 1

#if DEBUG_LEVEL > 5
    #define DBG_PRINT(fmt, ...) printf(fmt, __VA_ARGS__)
#elif DEBUG_LEVEL > 0
    #define DBG_PRINT(fmt, ...) fprintf(stderr, fmt, __VA_ARGS__)
#else
    #define DBG_PRINT(...)
#endif

// Token Pasting and Stringification
#define STR(x) #x
#define CONCAT(a, b) a ## b

#define GEN_VAR(name, suffix) CONCAT(name, suffix)

int GEN_VAR(counter, _01) = 0; // counter_01

// Variadic Macro for Flexible function definition
#define CALL_FUNC(func, ...) func(__VA_ARGS__)

// Compiler specific attributes
#if defined(_MSC_VER)
#define ALIGNED(x) __declspec(align(x))
#else
#define ALIGNED(x) __attribute__((aligned(x)))
#endif

ALIGNED(16) char buffer[32];
keywords: Advanced C preprocessor, Conditional compilation, C macro tricks, Token pasting
